editorial:
Imagine getting a guided tour of the Doctor's history from the man who actually lived it. You get to hang out with Jon Pertwee, who played the Third Doctor, as he looks back at his time in the TARDIS. Unlike earlier documentaries that had to deal with missing footage, you get the full experience here. The vibe is very cozy and nostalgic, feeling more like a chat with an old friend than a stiff history lesson. You'll see how the show changed when it moved to color and how the Doctor became more of an action hero who worked with Earth's military.

What really makes this special is seeing Pertwee's genuine love for his role and his funny stories about the set. The highlights are definitely the full clips from stories like Inferno and The Daemons, which show off the great acting and weird sci-fi ideas of the seventies. It is a bit slow if you want a movie with a plot, but for fans, it is gold.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by showing the final scenes of The Daemons, which was Pertwee's personal favorite. You see the Doctor successfully stop the alien threat and save the town. After the clips end, the film closes with a heartfelt reflection on the legacy of the Third Doctor. It ends by celebrating how Jon Pertwee changed the character forever before handing the keys of the TARDIS to the next Doctor.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Doctor Who or old TV history.
